newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks down on rising bad debt concerns.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks down on rising bad debt concerns.

text.p: Stocks of major Philippine banks slumped by midsession on Monday as reports of rising bad debts in the consumer banking sector further fuelled fears in an already skittish market, brokers said.
"There is now a cloud hanging over the banking sector due to the so-called defaults piling up in the credit card and consumer loans," Astro del Castillo, research analyst of A & A Securities said.
A foreign securities firm said some banks were facing default rates of over 12 percent in auto loans alone.

Leading the decline were Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co which fell 20 pesos to 650 pesos, Equitable Banking Corp which slid one peso to 114 pesos, and Philipine National Bank, which slipped 15 pesos to 290 pesos.

But Central Bank managing director for research Amando Tetangco said in a recent local television interview the latest survey on credit card and auto debt had so far not raised any red flags on the number of defaults.
"We do not think that the level of consumer lending has reached alarming levels," he said. Results of the survey should be out in the next few months.
The three banks were among the top ten most heavily traded issue on Monday.
